script: "I am 3 hours away from grandma, but her new husband's kids think I am the problem.". Oh my god, bestie, you won't believe the tea I am about to spill. I am literally about to lose my mind just thinking about this. So, my grandma has dementia, and my dad and I live three hours away, but we're always on the phone, helping her out. And we're not asking for anything in return, btw, just pure love. Now, her late husband's family is involved, and there's this one guy, B, who's super nice, but also super overbearing. He lives 30 minutes away from her and takes care of her... or so he thinks. Apparently, he's been taking money from her, bestie. Like, $10,000 checks with "vacation" scribbled on them, and two more checks for his own kids. My dad found this out, and, honestly, I am impressed. I would've flipped on the spot. My grandma said she didn't remember giving them the money, and when my dad asked about her bank accounts, she said B has full control. Like, what? I would be freaking out, but my dad's all calm and collected, right? Anyway, they started giving my dad the runaround, saying they're just helping, and if they help, they can take some money. Um, no, bestie, that's not how it works. And it gets worse. B deleted everything but Youtube from my grandma's TV, saying the news is too confusing for her. Like, who does that? My dad told him not to, but B just ignored him. My dad's had to repeatedly tell them to give them some space, but they just won't listen. They're like, "Oh, we're just helping," but really, they're controlling her life. So, my dad organized a dinner for my grandma's birthday, just for us, her, and a few close family members. He told B not to come, but B just showed up anyway, saying, "We're on our way." My dad's all like, "No, we just want it to be us," but B just ignores him. And, honestly, I think B's being super entitled. Like, respect my dad's boundaries, dude. Now, you're probably wondering if my dad's being the jerk for telling them not to come to the dinner. Honestly, I don't think so. I think they're being super overbearing and taking advantage of my grandma's dementia. And if my dad's trying to cut them off, I am all about it. Like, if they can't respect his boundaries, maybe they shouldn't be helping so much. Am I right, bestie?
